status: Protocols prepared for later prospective comparison; no workflow winner established
common_steps: Player outcome and fixed observation scope
Current implementation graph and source review

protocols.status: Initial baseline; resumed convoy work is a partial-history pilot
steps: Query affected atlas systems and function owners/callers/events
Record acceptance, invariants, cancellation/lifetime risks and unknowns
protocols.hypothesis: Tracing existing ownership before editing reduces integration mistakes and late special handling.
protocols.tradeoff: Static graphs can be stale or miss dynamic calls; reading huge inventories adds cost. Query narrowly and verify important edges in source.
protocols.basis: Our engineering adaptation of Godot scene ownership and the repository's existing atlas, not a standardized named method.

protocols.status: Candidate; compatible with current no-suite restriction
steps: Write the player story and its rules
For each important rule write concrete input/state/outcome examples
Separate unanswered questions and out-of-scope stories
Resolve material gameplay questions with Designer; freeze examples and implement the bounded feature
protocols.hypothesis: Concrete examples reduce ambiguity and prevent missed repeat/cancel/stale-state cases before coding.
protocols.tradeoff: Examples can miss lifecycle or resource-ownership hazards; the common graph review remains required. Large stories should be split rather than collect unlimited examples.
protocols.adaptation: Use written examples as planning artifacts now; do not install Cucumber, write regression suites or claim executable BDD adoption.

protocols.status: Candidate; compatible with current direct-check policy
steps: Perform the common graph review and draw the full intended connection
Choose the smallest genuine input-to-visible-result slice
Plan its ownership and failure boundaries before coding
Integrate that slice through real services and perform one permitted direct check
Plan the next slice from observed evidence; retain the original acceptance and all repair costs
artifacts: End-to-end graph with first slice highlighted
Versioned follow-on plan and common journal
protocols.hypothesis: Finding real integration failures early reduces the cost of connecting separately completed layers late.
protocols.tradeoff: Small-slice integration adds overhead, and an oversimplified slice can hide custody, cancellation or real UI problems. Do not replace real services with grants or fake successful outcomes.
protocols.basis: Adapted from Shape Up integrated slices and Pragmatic Programmer tracer-bullet guidance; not adoption of their full organizational process.

steps: Rank the few largest technical/behavioral unknowns by consequence and uncertainty
Sketch the interaction flow and explicit exclusions
Read engine documentation and investigate the highest-risk existing seam before implementation
Record significant choice as context-decision-consequences-status; freeze plan and build a bounded slice
artifacts: Short ranked risk list with evidence
One decision record only when architecturally significant
protocols.hypothesis: Resolving the largest known uncertainty before coding reduces abandoned implementations and costly architectural rework.
protocols.tradeoff: Risk analysis can consume the feature budget or rationalize speculation. Use an explicit planning appetite, keep normal reversible decisions local, and record unresolved unknowns honestly.
protocols.adaptation: A risky feasibility spike requires its own plan and permitted scoped evidence. No local engine or broad test campaign is implied, and a time appetite does not waive required behavior.

comparison_plan.status: Prepared only; no extra benchmark implementations authorized by this file
comparison_plan.unit: One bounded player-facing feature slice with versioned acceptance and comparable observation scope
start_conditions: Record feature size, affected owners and risk
Freeze protocol, acceptance, verification policy and source revision
State observation window for later reports
comparison_plan.assignment: Rotate protocols across comparable accepted feature slices. If replaying the same task later, use isolated identical baselines and record learning/order bias; do not replay in the shared game just to make a benchmark.
outcomes: Confirmed regressions and feature defects by severity with evidence
Planning-gap work and tracked repair time
Observed scope and open defect-reporting window
comparison_plan.analysis: Show individual runs, sample sizes, ranges and totals before aggregate comparisons. Do not rank unlike features as causal evidence, treat zero observations as proof, or optimize token count at the cost of correct gameplay.
comparison_plan.future_methods: TDD/automated BDD can be considered after the existing verification restriction changes; they are not silently approximated by running a renamed regression suite now.
